conversion_pathway.process: Form-dependent folate processing and folate-cycle conversion supply 5-methyltetrahydrofolate; folic acid requires reduction.
conversion_pathway.limitations: This conversion pathway does not show that increasing folate intake increases tissue remethylation flux. Folic acid lowers blood homocysteine, which is a circulating marker. The primary source is a biochemical review, not a new human flux study. Reaction identity does not show that ordinary dietary intake controls tissue remethylation rate, and it does not assign clinical benefit. Phosphatidylethanolamine methylation is a later SAMe-consuming reaction, not part of this step.

conversion_pathway.process: FLAD1 FAD synthase adenylates FMN with ATP to form FAD.

limitations: Foundational human-enzyme cofactor provenance supports capacity; it is not a measurement of dietary riboflavin-induced remethylation flux, brain methylation or benefit above adequacy. food_evidence.limitations: USDA FoodData Central reports choline in Broccoli, raw.

conversion_pathway.process: Choline oxidation supplies betaine upstream of BHMT.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. Human evidence is an eight-man depletion pilot, with the challenge response in four clinically depleted participants; tissue BHMT flux was not measured. Rat donor rescue and specific inhibition support the chain. This does not establish ordinary-diet limitation, response in every tissue or benefit above adequacy. Folate’s indirect constraint on BHMT remains unresolved. Choline oxidation can supply betaine, but increasing choline intake has not been shown to increase tissue BHMT flux. The enzyme evidence uses purified or recombinant human protein, not intact human metabolism. Loss of activity after removing zinc ligands does not show that dietary zinc usually limits the enzyme. The review statement that the pathway is independent of folate and vitamin B12 is not a new flux experiment. Quantitative claims in that review about choline deficiency and liver methionine were not re-checked in the primary animal papers. Purified, stable human choline dehydrogenase has been difficult to obtain, so some catalytic detail is inferred from related enzymes and from tissue activity rather than from a complete human kinetic characterisation. The reviews do not show that raising choline intake increases BHMT flux in people.

conversion_pathway.process: Protein digestion and amino-acid absorption provide methionine to the methionine cycle.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Dietary protein supplies methionine. It does not show that eating more protein increases cycle rates. DIAAS scores sulfur amino acids as methionine plus cysteine. The pathway accounts are reviews. Transsulfuration is not present in every tissue. The human rate study was a 28-day vitamin B6 restriction in nine healthy young adults. It does not show that ordinary changes in methionine, folate, or B-vitamin intake change those rates. Individual enzyme reactions remain neighbouring mechanisms.

records.food_material: Commercial liquid cow milk (31 samples: pasteurized, extended shelf-life and UHT)

food_evidence.evidence: Validated UHPLC measured native phosphorylated vitamers separately from unphosphorylated vitamers in commercial cow milk (Schmidt et al., 2017).
food_evidence.limitations: Verified qualitative vitamer occurrence. No individual amount is inferred from total vitamin B6 or B2. Preparation-specific concentrations are not transcribed. Food occurrence does not demonstrate intact cofactor delivery to the receiving tissue.

limitations: Purified-enzyme dependence on pyridoxal 5'-phosphate does not show that raising vitamin B6 intake increases cysteine formation in people. Moderate B6 restriction changed cystathionine handling but did not significantly reduce total transsulfuration in the assessed human tracer study.

food_evidence.limitations: USDA FoodData Central reports vitamin B6 in Bananas, raw.

conversion_pathway.process: Vitamer-specific endogenous activation; alternative ordered routes, not one chemical reaction
dependencies: PNPO and FMN for PNP/PMP routes
conversion_pathway.limitations: Alternative routes distinguish PL phosphorylation from PN/PM phosphorylation followed by oxidation. Total food vitamin B6 does not identify vitamer proportions, effective brain exposure or a predictable PLP yield.

evidence.statement: Human PDXK and PNPO enzymology supports distinct substrate-specific activation routes to the same canonical PLP target.

dependencies: ATP–divalent-metal substrate complex; metal effects depend on assay context
steps.limitations: PN and PM phosphorylation produces PNP and PMP, not PLP directly. In-vitro metal efficacy does not establish a dietary zinc requirement.

evidence.statement: Human PDXK phosphorylates PL, PN and PM to their respective 5-prime phosphates.

dependencies: ATP–divalent-metal substrate complex; metal effects depend on assay context
steps.limitations: PN and PM phosphorylation produces PNP and PMP, not PLP directly. In-vitro metal efficacy does not establish a dietary zinc requirement.

evidence.statement: Human PDXK phosphorylates PL, PN and PM to their respective 5-prime phosphates.

steps.limitations: Applies to phosphorylated PN/PM; PL does not require this oxidation step. Enzymology does not quantify neuronal PLP occupancy or food-level conversion yield.

evidence.statement: Human PNPO oxidises PNP and PMP to PLP with enzyme-bound FMN.

conversion_pathway.process: Methionine can supply cysteine through upstream transsulfuration before glutathione assembly.
conversion_pathway.limitations: A formula that removed methionine and cysteine together slowed whole-blood synthesis, so that result does not isolate methionine. In the cysteine-free study, methionine intake stayed adequate and red-cell synthesis did not fall. This does not show that eating more methionine, once intake is adequate, raises glutathione synthesis. All three studies measured blood-cell, not neuronal, synthesis. The sulfur-amino-acid-free diet was an experimental amino-acid formula in seven young men for 10 days. The older-adult increase required combined supplementation and was not an isolated N-acetylcysteine or glycine test, not an ADHD trial, and not ordinary food. The cysteine-free arm used only four young men and two days of adaptation. Concentration did not track synthesis rate in the sulfur-amino-acid-free study.

food_evidence.evidence: Intensifying sulforaphane formation in broccoli sprouts (2018)
food_evidence.limitations: Sulforaphane forms from glucoraphanin when sprouts are chopped or chewed; preparation affects the amount.

limitations: Human target engagement varies by formulation, tissue and population. The positive study used a myrosinase-completed broccoli sprout homogenate for three days in healthy nonsmokers and measured nasal phase II enzyme RNA, not Nrf2 protein or nuclear translocation. Extract capsules did not increase lung target-gene expression in COPD. An ordinary broccoli meal, direct activation of Nrf2 in the human brain and clinical ADHD benefit remain unestablished. Sulforaphane is not an essential nutrient.

conversion_pathway.process: Riboflavin kinase (RFK) phosphorylates riboflavin to FMN using ATP.

evidence.statement: Human RFK catalyses riboflavin phosphorylation; UniProt Q969G6 entry 195 retrieved 2026-10-26, Rhea 14357.

conversion_pathway.process: FLAD1 FAD synthase adenylates FMN with ATP to form FAD.
conversion_pathway.limitations: FAD production and enzyme loading depend on cellular context; no fixed food-to-FAD yield is inferred.

evidence.statement: Human FLAD1 catalyses FMN adenylation; UniProt Q8NFF5 entry 182 retrieved 2026-10-26, Rhea 17237.

limitations: Human red-cell enzyme evidence supports flavin-dependent capacity. It does not establish neuronal or whole-body recycling flux, benefit above adequacy, or equivalence between an ordinary food and a 5 mg/day supplement.

conversion_pathway.process: Multistep hepatic kynurenine/de-novo NAD metabolism and subsequent nicotinamide availability for salvage; not a direct one-step tryptophan-to-nicotinamide reaction.
conversion_pathway.limitations: Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺. This is a review of pathways, not a human feeding trial. It does not measure how much an ordinary meal changes NAD⁺, and it does not test attention or cognitive energy. Nicotinamide riboside and nicotinamide mononucleotide, as supplement doses, are outside this dietary assessment.

limitations: Most cells outside the liver do not run the full route. The review does not establish what share of the NAD⁺ pool comes from tryptophan, and eating more protein is not shown to raise NAD⁺.

conversion_pathway.process: Hepatic fatty-acid activation and successive mitochondrial beta-oxidation reactions generate acetyl-CoA from the C8 chain.

evidence.statement: Human medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase establishes the initial beta-oxidation reaction; the clinical exposure additionally measures downstream ketone provision.
